aiExplanation: This function finds the length of the longest subsequence of `nums` whose bitwise XOR is non-zero. It makes a single pass through the array, accumulating the XOR of all elements in `xor` and tracking with the boolean `allZeros` whether every element is `0` (using the `&&=` operator, which stays `true` only while each `num === 0`). It then applies three simple rules: if **all elements are zero**, no subsequence can ever produce a non-zero XOR, so it returns `0`; if the XOR of the **whole array is zero** (but not all elements are), dropping any single non-zero element makes the remaining XOR non-zero, so the answer is `nums.length - 1`; otherwise the entire array already has a non-zero XOR, so it returns `nums.length`.
